fieldValues.title: Escalation: may the release gate also run the RFC-043 arrangement fixture? (srs-rust#1481)
fieldValues.decision_question: May the release corpus-conformance gate gain the RFC-043 arrangement fixture, so that a failing arrangement scenario keeps a release in draft?
fieldValues.context: Problem: srs-rust#1481 runs the 14 RFC-043 arrangement scenarios against srs-rust, closing the gap srs-rust#793 closed for discovery. Its tests execute RFC-043's Conformance fixture section within the group's mandate, but one line of the PR adds the fixture to the release workflow's corpus-conformance gate. From then on a failing scenario stops a release from being promoted. The reviewer rejected it as an escalation, not a defect: anything touching a gate is outside the group's boundary. Why it matters: a release is what every client pins, so what blocks a release decides how early spec drift is caught against how often a release stalls. The change is small, but it widens what the gate refuses. Options and consequences: (A) Merge as is: drift between the spec's arrangement rules and the tool stops a release at once; a bad fixture would hold releases until fixed. (B) Split the workflow line into its own PR: the tests land now and run in CI; the gate change waits for a later ruling; nothing is blocked meanwhile. (C) Drop the workflow line and keep the tests only: drift shows in CI but never holds a release. Recommendation: B. Action needed: decide. Urgency: low; the PR is owner-merge and nothing is blocked by it. Answers: SP-01. Detail: https://github.com/the-greenman/srs-rust/pull/1481
fieldValues.friction: The tests are plainly within the ruling (RFC-043 Conformance fixture); the gate line is not covered by any recorded ruling. The reviewer cannot split a PR and the builder may not change what a gate refuses.
fieldValues.alternatives_considered: A. Merge as is. B. Split the gate line into its own PR. C. Keep the tests only and leave the release gate unchanged.
fieldValues.key_requirements: The arrangement fixture runs in CI. A change to what blocks a release is the owner's. The 14 scenarios stay the spec's, not the implementation's.
fieldValues.decision_statement: Land srs-rust#1481 without the release.yml line; ask for the gate change as a separate PR for the owner to merge once the fixture has been green on master for a while.
fieldValues.rationale: It gives the drift check now at no risk to releases, and keeps the one change that alters what a release needs under the owner's hand.
fieldValues.revisit_when: After the fixture has run green on master for a week, or the first time it catches real drift.
fieldValues.next_steps: Owner picks A, B or C on this record. If B, the builder removes the workflow line from srs-rust#1481 and files the gate change under SP-01.
